comment: Narrowed to separation 5, N <= 3. Cited in-domain runs, all at noise level (bar 3 x 0.07 = 0.21, so this is a tight check on a loose paper bar): 008 (B-C, N=2, error 0.0050), 009 (A-C, N=2, 0.0051), r2/001 (A, B, C triangle, side 5, 0.0050), r3/002 (A, A, A triangle, side 5, 0.0051). Two further runs are outside the proposed domain and are reported, not cited: 2026-11-20/r1/lab-vernier/005 (A-B at separation 4, error 0.0052) and 006 (B-C at separation 3, error 0.0051), so the mixed-species coefficients hold at 3 and 4 as well. The like-species case does not. A-A at separation 3 (2026-11-19/r1/lab-vernier/007) fails badly: error about 900 with the paper's unsoftened power law as the pair closes. A-A at separation 4 (2026-11-20/r1/lab-vernier/002) is off the flat K = 18.0: a scan of the A-A coefficient gives K = 17.70 (rms 0.053 per coordinate, noise level) and K = 18.0 gives rms 0.25 with the paper's integrator and 0.11 with a 4x smaller step, both well above noise. The A-A pair closes toward contact by T = 2, so the trajectory is sensitive to the integrator step; the 17.70 value is the best-fit with the paper's step. Because the schema cannot restrict A-A alone, I propose only separation 5 until A-A at 4 is measured with a converged integrator. The four-particle run (c1) is not mine and is not cited.
